 SpaceX secures $40B in financing for GPUs as Elon Musk warns of AI cloud industry consolidation
 Musk said debt markets have 'almost entirely shut off access to money' for companies without revenue beyond AI data centers
 Facebook 
 Twitter 
 Threads 
 Print 
 Email 
 Add Fox Business on Google 
 By Michael Sinkewicz FOXBusiness close video SpaceX revenue surges 161% as Elon Musk addresses potential Tesla merger 
 'The Big Money Show' panel discusses SpaceX reporting a 161% revenue increase as Elon Musk addresses a potential Tesla merger.
 Elon Musk said SpaceX has closed $40 billion in debt financing to purchase graphics processing units for its artificial intelligence operations, highlighting the enormous sums being spent in the race to build AI computing capacity.
 Musk announced the financing on Sunday, saying SpaceX was able to secure the money because of its investment-grade status and revenue generated outside AI through its Starlink satellite internet and rocket launch businesses.
 "SpaceX closed $40B of debt for GPUs, but we're investment grade and have Starlink & launch revenue," Musk said.
 Graphics processing units, or GPUs, are advanced chips that provide the computing power needed to train and operate AI systems.
 ELON MUSK SAYS TESLA VEHICLE DEMAND EXCEEDING PRODUCTION AHEAD OF DALLAS CYBERCAB LAUNCH 
 Elon Musk said SpaceX closed $40 billion in debt financing to purchase advanced computer chips for its artificial intelligence operations. (Francis Chung/Politico/Bloomberg via Getty Images / Getty Images) 
 Reuters previously reported that SpaceX was in talks with banks and asset managers to raise $40 billion to purchase Nvidia AI chips.
 "This is primarily callable debt for GPU purchases that will arrive in Q1 and Q2," Musk said in a follow-up post on X, confirming that the GPUs are expected to arrive in the first half of 2027. "Not a major factor this quarter."
 It was not immediately clear whether investors had agreed to the debt's pricing terms.
 The funding underscores the cost of the AI race, as companies spend heavily on advanced chips and other computing infrastructure.
 UKRAINE REGAINS CRITICAL STARLINK SERVICE AFTER RESTRICTIONS DISRUPT DRONE OPERATIONS 
 SpaceX CEO Elon Musk announced a $40 billion financing deal Sunday, citing the company's investment-grade status and revenue from Starlink and rocket launches. (Fabrice Coffrini / AFP via Getty Images / Getty Images) 
 SpaceX Chief Financial Officer Bret Johnsen said the company expects to spend $35 billion to $40 billion on capital expenditures in the fourth quarter alone, according to Reuters.
 Musk also said borrowing conditions have deteriorated significantly for companies that rely heavily on AI infrastructure .

 "As of the past few weeks, debt markets have almost entirely shut off access to money for any company that doesn't have substantial revenue independent of AI data centers," he said.
 Musk warned that many of those companies could struggle to survive.
 TRUMP PRAISES ELON MUSK AS A 'GENIUS' WHILE DEFENDING HIM AGAINST POTENTIAL DEMOCRATIC PROBES 
 Chief Technology Officer of X Elon Musk speaks at a conference on June 19, 2024, in Cannes, France. (Richard Bord/WireImage / Getty Images) 
 "That means the 200+ neoclouds are going to see guppy-level death and consolidation," Musk said, referring to companies that rent out computing power built primarily for AI customers. "Some will make it through, but not many."
 SpaceX's established businesses, including Starlink and rocket launches, provide revenue streams outside its AI operations.
 SpaceX's third-quarter revenue climbed 161% from a year earlier to $14.58 billion, according to Reuters.
 Musk suggested last week that a potential merger of Tesla and SpaceX would be "a good idea."

 He also said both companies have formed special committees of independent directors to explore a potential deal, though Musk stressed that a merger is not certain.
 Reuters contributed to this report.
